Article Title: Nepal flash floods: Relatives hold symbolic funerals for thousands missing as toll crosses 1,243
Article Text:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday.

The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday, as rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities along the Bhotekoshi River.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community, as families held symbolic funerals for relatives who remain missing following last week’s floods.Speaking at the fifth daily press briefing in Kathmandu, ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said authorities had begun conducting temporary burials for victims as search and rescue operations continued around the clock.Chhetri said 11,993 people had been rescued, while 1,114 bodies had been recovered. Around 3,900 people remain unaccounted for, he said, urging relatives of those missing to provide DNA samples at the Nepal Police Hospital in Maharajgunj or their nearest District Police Office to help forensic teams with identification.He also outlined international assistance being provided to Nepal. A 19-member forensic team from India is working with Nepal Police on DNA analysis, while specialised teams and equipment have also arrived from China, Singapore and South Korea to support identification and recovery efforts.Rescue teams from the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force are working with international specialists from India, China and South Korea to clear mud, debris and boulders from underground hydropower facilities in areas including Langtang, Chilime and Upper Trisuli.According to the ANI report, more than 300 foreign nationals have been safely rescued, while around 590 citizens from 34 countries remain unaccounted for.Working with Chinese authorities, Nepal has also helped evacuate about 2,500 pilgrims returning from Mount Kailash through the Hilsa and Tatopani border crossings and via air routes through Lhasa. Efforts are also underway to clear stranded cargo and assist Nepali nationals near the Kerung border.Addressing Parliament earlier Wednesday, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the catastrophic August 26 Bhotekoshi River floods, triggered by a high-altitude Himalayan avalanche, underscored the growing threat posed by climate change across the region.Shah said nearly 4,000 people remain missing across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, stressing that addressing the effects of climate change requires a collective global effort.As Nepal continues to coordinate international assistance from India, China, the United States, Japan, the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations, authorities are deploying available resources toward emergency relief, searches for missing people and long-term recovery.According to Nepal Police, 348 bodies were recovered in Chitwan, 217 in Nawalparasi East, 190 in Nawalparasi West and 155 in Nuwakot. Another 66 bodies were recovered in Gorkha, 59 in Dhading, 45 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahu.A total of 7,912 police personnel have been deployed to flood-hit areas to assist with search and rescue operations, distribute relief supplies and manage recovered bodies.Authorities have also published details of 911 unidentified bodies on the Nepal Police website to help families identify missing relatives.Meanwhile, rainwater accumulating inside a hydropower tunnel has created additional difficulties for search and rescue teams working in areas affected by the Bhotekoshi floods, said Dharma Raj Uprety, executive chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Search operations have been particularly challenging because of the hazardous conditions inside the project’s tunnels. Teams from the Nepali Army and Armed Police Force, along with foreign technical experts and project employees, are continuing efforts to locate workers who remain missing.As per the PTI report, Ganesh Karki, former president of the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), said rescue operations have also been slowed by difficulties transporting heavy equipment to the tunnels.
Article Summary: The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday. Rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities. Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community.

Article Title: Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours
Article Text:
Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours

Trump coin out of stock

Special law for Trump's portrait

It’s America’s 250th birthday, and Donald Trump is making sure he gets a spot on the souvenir.A new $1 coin marking the anniversary went on sale Wednesday with the president’s portrait on one side and the Great Seal of the United States on the other.The coins, issued by the US mint, can be used as legal tender. But their launch has also attracted criticism because federal law bars the depiction of a living president on US currency, although there are provisions allowing the Treasury Secretary to authorise special coins in certain circumstances.The coin’s design features Trump’s visage as “heads”, while the Great Seal of the United States serves as “tails”. Trump’s portrait carries the inscriptions “IN GOD WE TRUST” and “LIBERTY”, while “1776 (tilde) 2026” appears below his face.The reverse shows the Great Seal, with a bald eagle holding arrows in one claw and an olive branch in the other. A banner held in its beak carries the words “E PLURIBUS UNUM," Latin for "out of many, one.”The design received approval this year from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were appointed by Trump. The president had earlier called the idea of putting his face on a coin “very unusual”, but said he was “honored by it.”The US mint said the coins were struck to “honor 250 years of great American heritage.”The coins went on sale at noon Wednesday, but appeared to be out of stock by the afternoon.A roll of 25 coins costs $61, while a bag of 100 costs $154.50. At the same time, some special-issue coins had been randomly placed among the rolls and bags.The mint’s website later stated, “This item is available to be ordered now, but it is not currently in stock. Additional inventory is being made.”The 100-coin bag was listed as unavailable, while the 25-coin roll carried the same message shortly after 3pm.Just after 12.30pm, visitors to the website were placed in a waiting area with an estimated wait time of one hour. Purchases were limited to two per household until 2pm on Thursday, with buyers given 10 minutes to complete their orders.The website also warned, “Product availability is not guaranteed.” Furthermore, the coins would also be found in circulation, with the authority urging people to "check your pocket change.”Among the coins, 250,000 have been given a special-issue “July 4th” privy mark. Mint said that these coins were randomly included in the rolls and bags because they were struck on July 4, the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.Describing this as a “special offering”, the mint said, “250,000 Semiquincentennial President Donald J. Trump $1 Coins with a special-issue ‘July 4th’ privy mark have been randomly included in the Rolls & Bags. These coins were struck on July 4th.”Although the coin has a gold appearance, it is made from a mix of copper, zinc, manganese and nickel. Part of the additional cost of commemorative coins goes towards “organizations and projects that benefit the community”, according to the mint’s website.The use of Trump’s image on the coin comes despite US law prohibiting the display of a sitting president or living former president on US currency.In anticipation of America’s 250th anniversary, however, Congress passed the Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act. The legislation allows the US Treasury to mint special $1 coins to mark the event.The law also states, “No head and shoulders portrait or bust of any person, living or dead, and no portrait of a living person may be included in the design on the reverse of specified coins.”Trump’s portrait appears on the front of the coin, rather than the reverse, appearing to comply with the law.The treasury secretary also has authority in some circumstances to approve the minting and issuance of special coins.The only other time a living president was featured on a US coin was in 1926, when Calvin Coolidge appeared on a half dollar marking the 150th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, according to the mint.The coin is also part of a wider series of branding efforts associated with Trump’s second term that have become tangled up in lawsuits.These include moves to put Trump’s name on the Kennedy Center and the US Institute of Peace, as the president seeks to leave his stamp on history and Washington, DC.CNN reached out to the Treasury Department for information on the coins’ availability and the number of orders placed. It also sought information on where the surcharge money from the coins will go.
Article Summary: $1 coin features Donald Trump's portrait on one side, Great Seal of the United States on the other. The coins went on sale at noon Wednesday, but appeared to be out of stock by the afternoon. The use of Trump's image on the coin comes despite US law prohibiting the display of a sitting president or living former president on US currency.

Article Title: Delhi horror: Woman stabbed to death by boyfriend at hotel, accused attempts suicide
Article Text:
Woman was found dead at Prince Hotel room, discovered by staff in a disturbing scene involving a pool of blood





NEW DELHI: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly stabbed to death by her boyfriend at a hotel in Delhi’s Lahori Gate area, later man allegedly consumed poison in an apparent suicide attempt, police said on Thursday.The couple had checked into Hotel Prince on Wednesday evening. The man is a native of Rajasthan, while the woman was from Bihar, police said.Police said the man allegedly attacked the woman with a knife during the night, causing multiple injuries. He then consumed a poisonous substance and was taken to hospital for treatment.Hotel staff discovered the woman lying in a pool of blood inside the room on Thursday morning. She was taken to hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead. The accused is currently undergoing treatment, police said.The woman’s body has been sent for post-mortem examination and further investigation is underway.According to a police statement, Lahori Gate Police Station received information on Thursday morning about a man and a woman found unconscious at Hotel Prince."A police team immediately reached the spot, where a woman was found lying unconscious with multiple stab injuries.A man was also found unconscious at the same location," police said.Both were taken to a nearby hospital. The woman was declared brought dead, while the man remains under treatment, the officer said.Police are investigating the incident to establish the exact sequence of events and determine the circumstances that led to the woman’s death and the man’s alleged suicide attempt.
Article Summary: 28-year-old woman allegedly stabbed to death by her boyfriend at a hotel in Delhi. Man allegedly consumed poison in an apparent suicide attempt, police said. Hotel staff discovered the woman lying in a pool of blood inside the room. She was taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead.

Article Title: 2 students flying out to Russia from Mumbai for MBBS report Rs 6.5 lakh theft from bags; FIR registered
Article Text:
Mumbai airport (File Photo)





MUMBAI: Sahar police registered two FIRs against unidentified persons on Aug 31 after two Indian students pursuing MBBS in Russia reported US dollars equivalent to Rs 6.5 lakh stolen from their bags.The two travelled to Russian cities on separate flights from Mumbai on Aug 26 and 27. Police said these were the first theft cases involving international flights and have sought CCTV footage and details of airline ground staff at Mumbai airport.The families of the students said the cash, arranged through savings and loans, was meant for college fees and annual expenses.Priya Gavai (22) of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar reported $2,000, equivalent to around Rs 1.96 lakh, missing from her cabin bag after reaching Cairo on an EgyptAir flight to Moscow. Her mother, Seema Ingle (46), a schoolteacher, said airline staff had asked Gavai to place her purse in the cabin bag. She later handed it to a crew member because cabin storage space was unavailable. At Cairo airport, she found the lock broken and the currency missing.Ingle alleged airline staff were involved and said the airline had declined responsibility or reimbursement. She had saved money from her salary and borrowed Rs 2 lakh from a friend for her daughter’s fourth-year MBBS fees and expenses.In the second case, Sanika Rampurkar (19) of Ratnagiri reported $4,625, equivalent to around Rs 4.5 lakh, stolen while travelling to Adler on an Etihad Airways flight. Her flight, scheduled to travel via Abu Dhabi, was diverted to Istanbul.She reached Adler on Aug 27 but received her cabin and luggage bags on Aug 28. She found 46 $100 notes, one $20 note and one $5 note missing. Her father, Sachin Rampurkar (49), also a schoolteacher, said the money had been arranged through loans and savings for her medical college fees and annual expenses in Russia.A senior police officer said baggage theft investigations face logistical blind spots, including cargo loading and transit areas without direct camera surveillance. Reliance on outsourced loaders and third-party ground staff also makes identifying suspects difficult. Police suspect baggage scanning or handling staff may alert thieves about bags containing cash or gold.A Sahar police officer said they have sought details of the CCTV footage from both airlines at Mumbai airport when the passengers’ bags were scanned before loading into flight cargo sections. “Details of the ground staffs are sought to question to find involvement of them in the thefts,” the officer told TOI.
Article Summary: Two Indian students pursuing MBBS in Russia reported US dollars equivalent to Rs 6.5 lakh stolen from their bags. The two travelled to Russian cities on separate flights from Mumbai on Aug 26 and 27. Police said these were the first theft cases involving international flights.

Article Title: Op Sindoor commander Jeetendra Mishra selected as Ayodhya Ram temple’s first CEO
Article Text:
Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra (Retd) (File Photo)





LUCKNOW: Sixteen months after playing a key role in Operation Sindoor , the officer who commanded India’s western air operations has been chosen for a very different assignment. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has selected Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra (Retd) as the first chief executive officer (CEO) of the Ram temple in Ayodhya Mishra, who retired from the Indian Air Force in April 2026, will oversee the temple trust’s expanding administrative responsibilities. However, the standard operating procedure governing the appointment and functioning of the CEO is yet to be finalised, Trust general secretary Govind Dev Giri said.Speaking to TOI, Mishra said: “I came to know about my appointment through news reports. I am yet to receive any official communication from the Trust.”Mishra was Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7, 2025, in response to the Pahalgam terror attack . Much of the four-day air campaign was directed from the command rooms of the Western Air Command, one of the IAF’s most critical operational formations.As commander of the Western Air Command, Mishra oversaw decisions related to the deployment of aircraft and air defence assets during the operation. He was among the senior military leaders recognised for their role in the campaign and was awarded the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal by President Droupadi Murmu for distinguished service.His appointment brings to the Trust a leader with extensive experience in operational planning, logistics, coordination and management of large organisations.In a recent podcast, Mishra spoke about the air campaign during Operation Sindoor, describing how Indian forces identified and struck targets deep inside Pakistan. He underscored the importance of precision, technology and inter-service coordination. Several operational aspects of the campaign, however, remain classified.A native of Bhopatpura village in Deoria district of Uttar Pradesh, Mishra comes from a middle-class family. His father was a lecturer. He joined the National Defence Academy in 1983 and was commissioned as a fighter pilot in December 1986 before qualifying as an experimental test pilot, one of military aviation’s most specialised streams.During his career, he served as chief test pilot of both the Indian Air Force and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), flying aircraft in developmental and testing phases and evaluating systems before induction into service.Following the terrorist attack on the Pathankot airbase in January 2016, Mishra was tasked with taking charge of the station and strengthening its administrative and security framework. He later commanded the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment (ASTE) in Bengaluru, which works closely with HAL, the Defence Research and Development Organisation and civilian scientists.Mishra also spent three years at Air Headquarters in New Delhi, handling defence procurement. During that tenure, he was associated with nearly 75 projects and led the Air Force’s role in the first tranche of emergency procurements undertaken in 2019 and 2020.His professional training includes war management studies at the Air Command and Staff College in the United States and strategic studies at the Royal College of Defence Studies in London.The Trust’s CEO selection process began with 5,585 applications. A selection committee headed by retired Justice Permod Kohli and comprising Lt Gen VK Chaturvedi and nuclear scientist Suresh Haware conducted technology-assisted screening, verification and online assessments. The exercise was coordinated by the Trust secretariat under Sameer Panda.The pool was eventually narrowed to 16 candidates, who were interviewed in Ayodhya on Aug. 11 and 12. A panel of three names was submitted to the Trust on Sept. 1, after which Mishra was selected.As CEO, Mishra is expected to oversee the temple’s day-to-day administration, pilgrim facilities, financial arrangements, staff coordination and management of major religious events. The Trust will now finalise the CEO’s powers, responsibilities, reporting structure and service conditions before the appointment is formally operationalised.
Article Summary: Jeetendra Mishra (Retd) selected as first chief executive officer of the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Mishra was Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched in May 2025.

Article Title: Disha Salian death case: Cops had enough opportunity, but didn’t file FIR, says Bombay HC
Article Text:
Celebrity manager Disha Salian

Name no one withou grounds, says HC





MUMBAI: Bombay high court bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and R R Bhonsale said the Disha Salian case “investigation carried out by police raises more questions than it answers,” hence a CBI probe was necessary. HC had last Friday reserved for orders her father’s plea to probe the death as a murder, not suicide or accident. The father’s counsel, Nilesh Ojha, cited “suspicious circumstances” to seek a CBI probe as he argued her death was “the outcome of a deep-rooted conspiracy involving powerful people”.Interact with the family with sensitivity, HC directed CBI on Wednesday. Simultaneously, “care should be taken that no innocent person is harassed and the offenders, if any, are made to face the trial,” the judgment authored by Justice Kotwal said.After Disha’s father made allegations against Aaditya Th­ackeray, the Sena (UBT) neta intervened and through his senior counsel Sudeep Pasbola said the allegations against him were “motivated with mala fide intentions” when he was “neither directly nor ind­i­rectly connected with any all­e­ged offence.” Pasbola expr­e­ssed sympathy for Disha’s father, but said CBI cannot be directed to do a roving inquiry.Making no reference to names, HC said, “Nobody shall be treated as an accused unl­e­ss in the opinion of invest­iga­t­i­ng officer there are sufficient grounds to raise reason­a­ble suspicion against him de­pe­n­ding on the material co­lle­c­t­ed during the investigation.”The state and Pasbola said the father can file a private complaint before a magistrate for police to probe. HC said wi­th two probes that went on for almost six years, it would be improper to ask Salian to now seek a police probe order from a magistrate. The judges said Ojha is right, the magistrate has no power to direct CBI to investigate. HC held that police had sufficient opportunity, but didn’t register an FIR to conduct a thorough probe, instead they carried on a probe “inadequate and insufficient’’ in the facts of the case.HC said, “We have not made any observations again­st any particular individual. Th­at would be strictly within the realm of the investigation.”Kuldeep Patil, CBI couns­el, informed the court the ag­e­ncy had never thus far probed Disha’s death. HC, on being shown documents including the panchanama, photograp­hs of the body, and other details from the inquiry, raised questions on various aspects it fo­und “suspicious”, includi­ng whether injuries were consistent with a fall from such a height and details regarding clothes. Hiray argued the injuries included a skull fracture consistent with such a fall. He said neither parent raised “any suspicion’’ in their st­atements during two probes.Police conducted a probe under Section 174 of the erstwhile Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), a provision with “li­mited scope’’, the court said. The section is meant to find ‘cause of death’ when a death is reported as a suicide and an ADR is registered. Ojha argued for any suspicious death, po­lice were mandated to file an FIR and then investigate.“A probe under Section 174 of CrPC at the earliest to see whether registration of FIR is necessary,’’ HC said, “...to ensure that the evidence, if any, is not destroyed or doesn’t disappear due to passage of time. The investigation cannot go on for an inordinately long time. In the present case, the investigation was carried out in two stages and it went on for about six years. This is not the object of investigation under Section 174 of CrPC,’’ the judgment stressed. HC observed, “The case requires substantive investigation of a cognisa­ble offence.” If the probe reve­a­ls no offence, CBI is to file a closure report, HC directed, with Salian having a right to protest such closure.
Article Summary: Bombay high court bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and R R Bhonsale said the Disha Salian case “investigation carried out by police raises more questions than it answers’ The father’s counsel, Nilesh Ojha, cited “suspicious circumstances” to seek a CBI probe as he argued her death was “the outcome of a deep-rooted conspiracy involving powerful people”
